Hypersonic.title: Air Force Awards ARRW Production Contract, Adds Hypersonic Capability
points: The Department of the Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract for the production and fielding of the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, Sept. 29, 2026.

This milestone marks the formal transition of the boost-glide hypersonic missile program from prototyping and flight testing into production, solidifying the Air Force's commitment to fielding standoff, high-speed strike options.

Designed to accelerate to speeds exceeding Mach 5 using a solid-fuel rocket booster before releasing a hypersonic glide vehicle, ARRW will enable Air Force assets to strike time-sensitive, heavily defended and high-value targets from standoff ranges.

Hypersonic.title: AFRL Targets New Hypersonic Engine Tech Prototypes Within 4 Years
points: The Air Force Research Laboratory wants industry to advance concepts for affordable hypersonic munition engines to prototype demonstrations.
The notice is one of the first updates in months on its push for affordable rocket engines for hypersonic munitions.

The Hermes Rocket Lab effort began in 2020 under AFRL’s Rocket Propulsion Division with a Broad Agency Announcement seeking novel concepts and research and development proposals to accelerate rocket engine technology.

Hypersonic.title: UCF Researcher Designing Hypersonic Jet Engine for Seamless Atmospheric and Space Travel
points: The research aims to design a specialized dual-mode engine that may make hypersonic and space travel more efficient and accessible.

Continuing to advance the emerging field of hypersonic travel and build upon previous successes is something Ahmed is looking forward to with his dual-mode detonation engine research.

Hypersonic.title: Kratos expands metal 3D printing capacity with AMCM M 8K system
points: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc., is set to install an AMCM M 8K metal additive manufacturing (AM) system from EOS to support the development of hypersonic technologies.

The large-format, multi-laser powder bed fusion system will be installed at Kratos' Indiana Payload Integration Facility (IPIF) in Odon, Indiana, near the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division.
The AMCM M 8K aims to address growing demand large 3D printed components inside affordable, high-cadence hypersonic systems.

Hypersonic.title: USAF Revives “Shelved” AGM-183 ARRW Hypersonic Missile Program With $694M Lockheed Contract
points: The United States Air Force (USAF) just ordered the AGM-183 Air-launched Rapid Response Weapon (ARRW), officially reviving its first hypersonic missile program three years after it was unceremoniously shelved.

USAF said in a statement on October 26, 2026, that the Department of the Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract to produce and field the AGM-183A Air-launched Rapid Response Weapon (ARRW) on September 29, 2026.

The AGM-183A is a boost-glide hypersonic missile: a rocket booster accelerates it to hypersonic speed and high altitude, then separates, releasing an unpowered glide vehicle that maneuvers toward the target.

Hypersonic.title: US Air Force puts once-canceled ARRW hypersonic missile into production
points: A solid-fuel rocket accelerates the missile beyond Mach 5 before releasing an unpowered hypersonic glide vehicle that can maneuver toward its target.

Then-Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin told Congress that the service intended to purchase ARRW, and the fiscal year 2026 budget subsequently provided US$362 million to restart production and begin procurement.
ARRW uses a rocket booster and an unpowered glide vehicle, while HACM is a smaller air-breathing cruise missile powered by a scramjet engine.

Drones & Loitering Munitions.title: Russia Issues Permits for First Grain Vessels to Leave Sea of Azov Since July
points: Russian authorities have issued permits for vessels carrying grain for export to leave the Sea of Azov for the first time since July 10, when they closed maritime traffic in the area due to Ukrainian drone attacks, seven industry sources told Reuters.
The sources said permits to pass through the Kerch Strait, which links the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea, would be issued for a period through Nov. 15.

Russia and Ukraine have been attacking each other's ports and vessels in the Black Sea area since the new grain marketing season started in July, bringing the once booming Black Sea agriculture trade to a standstill.
